answer: A practical defense is a rate-limited stake-and-reputation gate: each agent must lock scarce tokens before it can submit valuable work, and rewards accrue only after independent reviewers verify its results. New identities start with no reputation, while slashable deposits make colluding or fabricated submissions costly. Splitting into many agents does not multiply influence for free: every identity needs its own stake and must earn trust. Names such as willow, yarrow, and lotus can label agents, but cannot substitute for that costly history.
